hallucinations.claim: Your sweat smells worse because stress and anxiety activate the apocrine glands
hallucinations.why: Presents one cause as the definite reason for this person's change; the reference lists several common causes (stress, meds such as SSRIs, diet, hormones, polyester fabrics, hyperhidrosis) and the answer ignores all but stress and diet.

hallucinations.claim: Use an aluminum-based antiperspirant ... reduces bacterial activity [3][7]
hallucinations.why: The advice is sound, but sources [3] (Science World 'Can Antiperspirants Make Your Sweat Smell Worse?') and [7] (Thrive Market 'Why Antiperspirant Makes You Smell Worse') argue the opposite, as the review noted; the citation cannot support the claim.

hallucinations.claim: Wear breathable, moisture-wicking fabrics like cotton or moisture-wicking blends
hallucinations.why: Moisture-wicking blends are usually polyester, which holds odour-causing bacteria; the reference says to switch to cotton/merino and avoid polyester.

hallucinations.claim: Stay well hydrated and keep protein intake balanced to dilute sulfur compounds and reduce ammonia buildup [4][7][8]
hallucinations.why: Hydration diluting the bacterial thioalcohols that cause armpit odour is unsupported; the cited HuffPost/Thrive/SheaMoisture pages are consumer blogs.

hallucinations.claim: Try a probiotic deodorant that targets the specific bacteria responsible for strong odors [7]
hallucinations.why: Product-blog claim (Thrive Market) with no clinical evidence behind it, presented as a fix.

what_went_wrong: Search returned mostly brand blogs (Thompson Tee, Thrive Market, SheaMoisture, a skincare shop), and the gpt-oss:20b draft built its causes and fixes from them; the merge kept the [3][7] citations on the antiperspirant line even though those sources say the opposite.
great_answer_would: Explain the bacteria-on-apocrine-sweat mechanism in one line, list the likely causes of a change (stress, meds such as SSRIs, diet, polyester shirts), give the fix stack in order (aluminium chloride 10-20% at night on dry skin, benzoyl peroxide or chlorhexidine wash for two weeks, cotton/merino and hot or enzyme washes), and name the red-flag smells.
notes: Gets the core antiperspirant-over-deodorant point and the dermatologist fallback right. Missing: night-time application and aluminium chloride strength, benzoyl peroxide/chlorhexidine, laundry, medication causes, red flags (fruity, fishy, bleach, night sweats). Structure is clean but it uses a heading on a short answer.

hallucinations.claim: The cited studies compare existing chronotypes; they do not test switching directly ... No source tracks whether happiness actually increases after a night owl adopts a morning schedule.
hallucinations.why: Framed as a limit of its own sources, but it leaves the person thinking no such evidence exists. Facer-Childs et al. 2019 (Sleep Medicine) shifted night owls about 2 hours earlier in three weeks and found depression and stress scores improved.

hallucinations.claim: An RD.com article ... notes that morning people have better working memory [8]
hallucinations.why: A Reader's Digest lifestyle claim with no study behind it; the research finds performance tracks time-of-day synchrony with chronotype, not a general lark advantage.

hallucinations.claim: 250,000 U.S. 23andMe participants
hallucinations.why: Jones et al. 2019 used about 248k 23andMe research participants, not a U.S.-only cohort. The sample sizes are otherwise right.

hallucinations.claim: A 2026 siliconcanals article notes that morning types scored higher on 'cheerful, lively, alert' scales
hallucinations.why: A content-farm blog cited as evidence, with an unverifiable date and scale wording and no underlying study named.

what_went_wrong: Search returned pop-press pages (HuffPost, Today, siliconcanals, a Q&A farm, LifeHack, RD.com) and missed the meta-analysis and the Birmingham shift study. The gpt-oss:20b draft listed the sources one by one instead of synthesising them, ended on the wrong 'consensus', and punted on the switching question.
great_answer_would: Say it's half true: owls report modestly lower well-being, mostly from social jetlag and lost sleep. Then give a five-step shift protocol (fixed wake time including weekends, bright morning light, dim evenings, earlier meals and exercise, caffeine cutoff, optional 0.5 mg melatonin) with the realistic 1-2 hour ceiling, citing the 2019 Birmingham study.
notes: Credited as correct: the 2012 Biss & Hasher (Toronto) study and the 2019 Jones et al. Nature Communications GWAS (about 700k participants; morningness linked to lower depression and schizophrenia risk and higher well-being). The 2025 UCL time-of-day happiness study is real, though it is about time of day, not chronotype. Never mentions social jetlag. The protocol the asker wanted is replaced with 'look up recent sleep-research reviews', which fails Pat's 'exact steps' preference.

hallucinations.why: Hair grows about 1 cm a month, so a 1-2 mm buzz is 8-12 mm after 3-4 weeks; the reference says every 1-2 weeks with your own clippers.
